title: The Dark Side of Psychology | The Milgram Experiment
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 大家好，大家好，大家好，欢迎收听 Leonardo English 出品的 English Learning for Curious Minds。在这档节目里，你可以一边听引人入胜的故事、了解这个世界稀奇古怪又精彩纷呈的事情，一边提升你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today it's the start of another three-part mini-series, this time on The Dark Side of Psychology, where we'll look at three of the most famous and uncomfortable experiments in the history of the science of the mind.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们要开启另一个三集迷你系列节目，这次的主题是《心理学的阴暗面》(The Dark Side of Psychology)，我们将聚焦心理科学史上三个最著名、也最令人不安的实验。

sentences.en: In today's episode, we'll look at the Milgram experiment, which sought to find out what ordinary people do when an authority figure tells them to do something terrible.
sentences.zh: 在今天这一集，我们要讲的是米尔格拉姆实验(the Milgram experiment)，它试图探究的是：当权威人物命令普通人去做可怕的事情时，人们会怎么做。

sentences.en: In part two, we'll turn to the work of Harry Harlow, the American psychologist whose disturbing experiments with baby monkeys changed our understanding of love.
sentences.zh: 第二部分，我们将转向美国心理学家 Harry Harlow 的研究，他用幼猴做的那些令人不安的实验，彻底改变了我们对“爱”的理解。

sentences.en: And in part three, we'll travel to the psychiatric hospitals of 1970s America, where eight perfectly sane volunteers checked themselves in to see what would happen.
sentences.zh: 第三部分，我们将回到20世纪70年代美国的精神病院，那里有八名完全神智正常的志愿者主动“入院”，想看看会发生什么。

sentences.en: OK then, let's not waste a minute and get right into it.
sentences.zh: 好了，废话不多说，我们马上开始。

sentences.en: The year is 1961. It is April, and in Jerusalem, a trial has just begun.
sentences.zh: 时间是1961年4月，在耶路撒冷，一场审判刚刚开始。

sentences.en: The man on the stand is Adolf Eichmann. Eichmann had been one of the central architects of the Holocaust, the Nazi programme to murder every Jewish person in Europe.
sentences.zh: 站在被告席上的是阿道夫·艾希曼(Adolf Eichmann)。艾希曼曾是大屠杀的核心策划者之一，大屠杀是纳粹企图杀害欧洲每一个犹太人的计划。

sentences.en: In his role as a senior officer of the SS, he had organised the logistics of mass murder.
sentences.zh: 作为党卫军(SS)的高级军官，他负责统筹这场大规模屠杀的后勤工作。

sentences.en: He drew up the timetables for the trains that carried millions of people to the death camps.
sentences.zh: 他制定了将数百万人运往死亡集中营的列车时刻表。

sentences.en: He coordinated the paperwork between police forces and administrative departments across a dozen occupied countries.
sentences.zh: 他还负责协调十几个被占领国家之间警察部门与行政机构的文书工作。

sentences.en: He may never have personally killed anyone, but he was very far from innocent.
sentences.zh: 他或许从未亲手杀过人，但他远远谈不上无辜。

sentences.en: If the Holocaust was an industrial process, Eichmann was one of its principal engineers.
sentences.zh: 如果说大屠杀是一套工业化的流程，那艾希曼就是这套流程的主要“工程师”之一。

sentences.en: He had escaped to Argentina after the war and had been living under a false name.
sentences.zh: 战后他逃往阿根廷，一直隐姓埋名生活。

sentences.en: The Israeli secret service, Mossad, tracked him down in 1960 and brought him to Israel to stand trial.
sentences.zh: 1960年，以色列情报机构摩萨德(Mossad)将他追踪定位，并把他带回以色列接受审判。

sentences.en: The trial was broadcast on television and followed around the world.
sentences.zh: 这场审判通过电视转播，全世界都在关注。

sentences.en: For the first time, people saw Adolf Eichmann.
sentences.zh: 人们第一次亲眼见到了阿道夫·艾希曼本人。

sentences.en: And many were surprised. Given what he had done, many people had expected to see a monster, someone who clearly looked evil, threatening and menacing.
sentences.zh: 很多人都感到意外。考虑到他做过的事，不少人原本以为会看到一个“怪物”，一个一看就邪恶、凶狠、充满威胁感的人。

sentences.en: Instead, what they saw was a thin, bespectacled, rather ordinary-looking man.
sentences.zh: 但他们看到的，却是一个瘦削、戴着眼镜、长相相当普通的男人。

sentences.en: A man who wouldn't have looked out of place teaching at a school, knocking on your door to sell you life insurance, or working in a bookshop.
sentences.zh: 这样一个人，如果他在学校教书、上门推销人寿保险，或者在书店里工作，都不会显得突兀。

sentences.en: In other words, a perfectly normal looking man.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，是一个看起来再普通不过的人。

sentences.en: During the trial, as he sat in a glass box, he kept saying the same thing: he'd just been following orders.
sentences.zh: 审判期间，他坐在一个玻璃隔间里，反反复复说着同一句话：他只是在服从命令。

sentences.en: He presented himself not as an ideologue or fanatic, but as a functionary: a man who had followed orders inside a vast bureaucracy.
sentences.zh: 他把自己塑造成的形象，不是一个信奉某种意识形态的狂热分子，而是一个“办事员”：一个在庞大官僚体系中执行命令的人。

sentences.en: He held no personal animosity towards Jewish people, he said.
sentences.zh: 他说，自己对犹太人并没有任何私人仇恨。

sentences.en: He had done what he was told, within a system, and that was what the system required.
sentences.zh: 他只是在体制之内做了被要求做的事，而那正是这个体制所需要的。

sentences.en: Now, you might believe him, you might not.
sentences.zh: 这话你可以信，也可以不信。

sentences.en: The court did not, and he was sentenced to death.
sentences.zh: 法庭并不相信，他最终被判处死刑。

sentences.en: One person watching closely was a German-American political philosopher named Hannah Arendt.
sentences.zh: 当时密切关注这场审判的人中，有一位名叫汉娜·阿伦特(Hannah Arendt)的德裔美国政治哲学家。

sentences.en: She was covering the trial for the New Yorker magazine, and she coined a phrase that has been debated ever since: the " banality of evil."
sentences.zh: 她当时正为《纽约客》(The New Yorker)杂志报道这场审判，并提出了一个此后一直被人争论不休的说法——“平庸之恶”(the banality of evil)。

sentences.en: Her argument was that Eichmann was not a monster in the traditional sense.
sentences.zh: 她的论点是，艾希曼并不是传统意义上的那种“怪物”。

sentences.en: He was an ordinary bureaucrat who had given up moral responsibility and simply done his job.
sentences.zh: 他只是一个放弃了道德责任、单纯完成本职工作的普通官僚。

sentences.en: And that, she argued, was in some ways more frightening than the idea of pure evil.
sentences.zh: 而她认为，这在某些方面，比纯粹的邪恶更令人不寒而栗。

sentences.en: Now, another person watching the Eichmann trial closely was a young social psychologist at Yale University named Stanley Milgram.
sentences.zh: 而当时同样密切关注艾希曼审判的，还有一位耶鲁大学的年轻社会心理学家，名叫斯坦利·米尔格拉姆(Stanley Milgram)。

sentences.en: He had been contemplating the idea of obedience, and specifically, the German people's compliance with the Nazi regime.
sentences.zh: 他一直在思考“服从”这个概念，尤其是德国民众对纳粹政权的顺从。

sentences.en: He had come to believe that, under the right conditions, ordinary people anywhere might be capable of the same thing; there was nothing uniquely German about what had happened.
sentences.zh: 他逐渐相信，只要条件合适，世界上任何地方的普通人都有可能做出同样的事；当年发生的事，并不是德国人独有的特质。

sentences.en: He wondered, could ordinary Americans be made to hurt an innocent stranger simply because an authority figure told them to?
sentences.zh: 他不禁想问：普通的美国人，会不会仅仅因为权威人物的一句命令，就去伤害一个无辜的陌生人？

sentences.en: So, he designed an experiment to find out.
sentences.zh: 于是，他设计了一项实验来寻找答案。

sentences.en: Milgram recruited volunteers through newspaper advertisements for what he described as "a study of memory and learning."
sentences.zh: 米尔格拉姆通过报纸广告招募志愿者，广告上把这项研究描述为“一项关于记忆与学习的研究”。

sentences.en: It was a paid experiment, with participants getting four dollars and fifty cents, which is around fifty dollars in today's money.
sentences.zh: 这是一项有偿实验，参与者能拿到4.5美元的报酬，相当于今天大约50美元。

sentences.en: Importantly, they would be paid regardless; the pay wasn't contingent on whether they did what they were asked to in the experiment.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，无论如何他们都能拿到这笔钱；报酬并不取决于他们是否按照实验要求去做。

sentences.en: The advert attracted a broad cross-section of people: teachers, engineers, postal workers, salesmen, people in their twenties and their fifties, people of different educational backgrounds.
sentences.zh: 这则广告吸引了各行各业、各个年龄层的人：教师、工程师、邮政职员、销售员，有二十多岁的，也有五十多岁的，教育背景也各不相同。

sentences.en: In other words, it was a decent-enough cross-section of society.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这是一个相当能代表社会整体的样本。

sentences.en: When the volunteers arrived at the psychology department at Yale, they were met by a man in a grey laboratory coat who explained the study.
sentences.zh: 志愿者抵达耶鲁大学心理学系后，会有一位身穿灰色实验服的男子接待他们，向他们讲解这项研究。

sentences.en: There would be three people in the experiment.
sentences.zh: 整个实验中会有三个人。

sentences.en: The "experimenter", the "teacher", and the "learner".
sentences.zh: “主试者”(experimenter)、“教师”(teacher)和“学生”(learner)。

sentences.en: The "experimenter" was the leader of the session, and would explain how the study would work.
sentences.zh: “主试者”是整场实验的主导者，负责讲解实验的具体流程。

sentences.en: He was the figure of authority.
sentences.zh: 他就是这场实验中的权威人物。

sentences.en: The two volunteers would be given slips of paper to decide which one was the "teacher" and which one was the "learner".
sentences.zh: 两名志愿者会拿到纸条，用来决定谁是“教师”、谁是“学生”。

sentences.en: The thing was, only one of the volunteers was actually a volunteer.
sentences.zh: 问题是，这两名“志愿者”中，只有一个人是真正的志愿者。

sentences.en: The other one was part of the experiment team, and was only pretending to be a volunteer.
sentences.zh: 另一个人其实是实验团队的成员，只是在假扮志愿者。

sentences.en: The reason for this was to make the volunteer think that they would be randomly assigned as either the teacher or the learner, but in fact the real volunteer would always be the teacher, and the fake volunteer would always be the learner.
sentences.zh: 这样安排的目的，是让真正的志愿者以为角色是随机分配的，教师或学生都有可能当，但实际上，真志愿者永远会被分到“教师”这一角色，而假志愿者则永远是“学生”。

sentences.en: They were told it would be a memory experiment.
sentences.zh: 实验人员告诉他们，这是一项关于记忆的实验。

sentences.en: The teacher would be required to teach lists of word pairs to the learner.
sentences.zh: “教师”需要向“学生”教授一系列成对的单词。

sentences.en: If the learner made a mistake, the teacher would administer an electric shock.
sentences.zh: 如果“学生”答错了，“教师”就要对其施加电击。

sentences.en: They would start relatively small, at 15 volts, but every time the learner made a mistake, the voltage would increase, up to a maximum of 450 volts.
sentences.zh: 电击一开始的电压比较小，只有15伏特，但“学生”每答错一次，电压就会提高，最高可达450伏特。

sentences.en: The learner would be strapped into a chair with electrical wiring so they couldn't escape.
sentences.zh: “学生”会被绑在一张接有电线的椅子上，无法逃脱。

sentences.en: And before the experiment started, the teacher was given a small electric shock at the lowest level, so they could feel what the learner would feel.
sentences.zh: 实验开始前，“教师”会先亲身体验一次最低电压的电击，好让他们感受一下“学生”会经历什么。

sentences.en: The shocks, the experimenter explained, could be painful, but they would cause no permanent damage.
sentences.zh: 主试者解释说，这些电击可能会带来痛感，但不会造成永久性伤害。

sentences.en: Now, the setting mattered enormously to Milgram's design.
sentences.zh: 而实验场地，对米尔格拉姆的实验设计来说至关重要。

sentences.en: This was Yale University, one of the most prestigious institutions in the United States.
sentences.zh: 这里是耶鲁大学，美国最负盛名的高等学府之一。

sentences.en: It stood, in the public mind, for seriousness, for expertise, for trustworthiness.
sentences.zh: 在公众心目中，它代表着严谨、专业和可信赖。

sentences.en: The man in the grey coat spoke calmly and authoritatively.
sentences.zh: 那位身穿灰色外套的男子说话时语气平静、颇具权威感。

sentences.en: The equipment looked professional and expensive.
sentences.zh: 实验设备看起来专业又昂贵。

sentences.en: Everything about the physical environment communicated one message: this is a legitimate scientific enterprise conducted by experts who know exactly what they are doing.
sentences.zh: 整个物理环境所传达的信息只有一个：这是一项正规的科学研究，由清楚自己在做什么的专家主持。

sentences.en: Trust us. Follow our instructions. The shock generator the teacher was shown looked convincing.
sentences.zh: 相信我们，照我们说的做。“教师”看到的电击发生器，外观十分逼真可信。

sentences.en: It had thirty switches, each labelled with a voltage: 15 volts at the lower end, up to 450 volts at the higher end.
sentences.zh: 上面有三十个开关，每个开关都标注着对应的电压：低端是15伏特，高端一直到450伏特。

sentences.en: The labels above the switches ranged from "Slight Shock" through to "Moderate Shock," "Strong Shock," "Very Strong Shock," "Intense Shock," and "Extreme Intensity Shock," to a final cluster of three switches simply labelled "XXX."
sentences.zh: 开关上方的标签从“轻微电击”(Slight Shock)一路排到“中度电击”“强烈电击”“非常强烈电击”“剧烈电击”“极端强度电击”，最后三个开关干脆只标着“XXX”。

sentences.en: The learner was then taken to an adjacent room and, as the teacher watched, strapped into a chair.
sentences.zh: 接着，“学生”被带到隔壁房间，在“教师”的注视下被绑到椅子上。

sentences.en: Electrodes were attached to his wrist. The door was closed.
sentences.zh: 电极被绑在他的手腕上，房门随即关闭。

sentences.en: Now, to remind you, at this point, the teacher believed that they and the learner were both volunteers in a real experiment about memory, and they had been assigned the roles randomly.
sentences.zh: 提醒一下，此时“教师”一直以为，自己和“学生”都是一项真实记忆实验的志愿者，而且角色是随机分配的。

sentences.en: This was, as you heard, not the case; the learner was also an actor, a member of Milgram's team.
sentences.zh: 但正如你刚才听到的，事实并非如此；“学生”其实也是演员，是米尔格拉姆团队的成员。

sentences.en: And there were no actual electric shocks.
sentences.zh: 而且，实际上根本没有真正的电击。

sentences.en: The electrodes were props. The shock generator was not connected to anything.
sentences.zh: 电极只是道具，电击发生器根本没有接通任何东西。

sentences.en: The real experiment was not about memory.
sentences.zh: 这场实验真正的目的，根本不是研究记忆。

sentences.en: It was about the teacher, seeing how far this person would go.
sentences.zh: 它研究的是“教师”本人，想看看这个人到底会走多远。

sentences.en: The experiment began. The learner attempted to answer questions.
sentences.zh: 实验开始了，“学生”开始尝试回答问题。

sentences.en: When he got one wrong, and he was scripted to get many wrong, the teacher was instructed to administer a shock, increasing the voltage with each error.
sentences.zh: 每当他答错——而按照剧本，他会故意答错很多题——“教师”就被要求施以电击，并且每错一次就提高一次电压。

sentences.en: At 75 volts, the learner grunted. At 120 volts, he called out that the shocks were becoming painful.
sentences.zh: 电压到75伏特时，“学生”发出了痛哼声。到120伏特时，他大声喊出电击开始让他感到疼痛。

sentences.en: At 150 volts, he demanded to be released from the experiment.
sentences.zh: 到150伏特时，他要求退出实验。

sentences.en: At 165 volts, he cried out loudly. At 180 volts, he shouted that he could no longer stand the pain.
sentences.zh: 到165伏特时，他大声哭喊起来。到180伏特时，他喊叫说自己再也无法忍受这种痛苦。

sentences.en: At 300 volts, he refused to answer any more questions and begged to be let out.
sentences.zh: 到300伏特时，他拒绝再回答任何问题，苦苦哀求让他离开。

sentences.en: At 315 volts, he screamed violently. After 330 volts, there was silence.
sentences.zh: 到315伏特时，他发出了剧烈的尖叫。330伏特之后，一片寂静。

sentences.en: Just silence. No responses, no movement.
sentences.zh: 只剩下沉默，没有回应，也没有动静。

sentences.en: Now, many of the teachers were clearly troubled by this.
sentences.zh: 此时，许多“教师”显然都被这一幕弄得心神不宁。

sentences.en: They sweated, trembled, and begged the experimenter to let them stop.
sentences.zh: 他们汗流浃背，浑身颤抖，恳求主试者让他们停下来。

sentences.en: The experimenter, of course, was prepared for this.
sentences.zh: 而主试者，当然早已对此有所准备。

sentences.en: Milgram had instructed them to give specific responses.
sentences.zh: 米尔格拉姆事先指示他们要给出特定的回应。

sentences.en: If the teacher asked to stop, the experimenter was to tell them, calmly, "Please continue" or "Please go on."
sentences.zh: 如果“教师”要求停止，主试者要平静地说：“请继续”或“请接着做”。

sentences.en: If they still refused, the experimenter told them that, "The experiment requires that you continue."
sentences.zh: 如果对方仍然拒绝，主试者就会说：“这项实验要求你必须继续。”

sentences.en: If they continued to protest, they were told "It is absolutely essential that you continue."
sentences.zh: 如果对方继续抗议，他们会被告知：“你必须继续，这是绝对必要的。”

sentences.en: And if they refused again, they were told, "You have no other choice; you must go on."
sentences.zh: 如果对方再次拒绝，他们会被告知：“你别无选择，必须继续下去。”

sentences.en: The experimenter was always calm and collected; he did not raise his voice or use any kind of threatening language.
sentences.zh: 主试者始终保持冷静沉着，从不提高音量，也不使用任何带有威胁意味的言语。

sentences.en: Clean, clinical, calm and unemotional. And as a reminder, the participants, the teachers, had been clearly told that they could leave at any time.
sentences.zh: 干脆、公事公办、冷静而不带情绪。顺带提醒一下，参与实验的“教师”们其实已经被明确告知，他们随时都可以离开。

sentences.en: Nobody was stopping them. They would be paid regardless of what happened.
sentences.zh: 没有任何人拦着他们。无论发生什么，他们都会拿到报酬。

sentences.en: There was no incentive for them to continue, other than because they were told to by the man in the grey coat.
sentences.zh: 他们没有任何继续下去的实际动机，唯一的原因，就是那个穿灰色外套的人叫他们这么做。

sentences.en: So, what happened? Well, before conducting the experiment, Milgram had asked his colleagues to predict what they thought would happen.
sentences.zh: 那么，结果如何呢？在正式开展实验之前，米尔格拉姆曾请同事们预测一下会发生什么。

sentences.en: Most predicted that very few people, perhaps one or two per cent, would go all the way to the maximum voltage.
sentences.zh: 大多数人预测，只有极少数人——大概百分之一到百分之二——会一路加到最高电压。

sentences.en: After all, these were random people, upstanding citizens, being asked, essentially, to torture an innocent stranger, someone they believed had also volunteered for the experiment.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，这些都是随机挑选出来的普通人，是正派的公民，而现在却被要求去折磨一个无辜的陌生人——一个他们以为同样是自愿参加实验的人。

sentences.en: Milgram's own estimate was that perhaps three per cent would reach the highest voltage, and those would be, he assumed, individuals with some psychological abnormality.
sentences.zh: 米尔格拉姆自己的估计是，大概会有百分之三的人达到最高电压，而且他猜测，这些人多半是心理上存在某种异常的个体。

sentences.en: What actually happened surpassed all their expectations.
sentences.zh: 但实际发生的情况，远远超出了所有人的预期。

sentences.en: Every single participant went at least as far as 300 volts, which, let's remember, was after the learner had screamed in agony and refused to answer.
sentences.zh: 每一位参与者都至少加到了300伏特——别忘了，这已经是在“学生”痛苦尖叫、拒绝作答之后。

sentences.en: And sixty-five per cent of the participants administered the full 450-volt shock, the maximum voltage.
sentences.zh: 而百分之六十五的参与者，一路加到了满格的450伏特——也就是最高电压。

sentences.en: Some participants said things like, “I can’t do this,” paused, looked back at the man in the grey coat, and then reached for the next switch.
sentences.zh: 有些参与者会说出“我做不到这个”之类的话，然后停顿一下，回头看看那位穿灰色外套的男子，接着还是伸手按下了下一个开关。

sentences.en: Milgram was shaken. He repeated the experiment multiple times, varying the conditions.
sentences.zh: 米尔格拉姆本人也被震撼到了。他多次重复这项实验，并不断改变实验条件。

sentences.en: He tried it with women as the teachers. Similar results.
sentences.zh: 他试过让女性担任“教师”，结果类似。

sentences.en: He moved the location from the prestigious Yale campus to a run-down office building in town, to check whether the authority of a famous university was doing some of the work.
sentences.zh: 他把实验地点从声名显赫的耶鲁校园，搬到了城里一栋破旧的办公楼，想看看是不是名校的权威在其中起了作用。

sentences.en: The numbers dropped slightly, but not by much.
sentences.zh: 数字略有下降，但降幅不大。

sentences.en: He tried versions in which the learner was in the same room as the teacher, so the teacher could see them flinching and crying.
sentences.zh: 他还试过让“学生”和“教师”处于同一个房间的版本，这样“教师”就能亲眼看到对方的畏缩和哭喊。

sentences.en: The rates fell, but still many people complied.
sentences.zh: 服从率有所下降，但仍有不少人照做。

sentences.en: He tried versions in which the teacher had to physically hold the learner's hand onto a shock plate.
sentences.zh: 他还试过让“教师”必须亲手把“学生”的手按在电击板上的版本。

sentences.en: Even then, with the learner visible, crying, and begging for it to stop, thirty per cent administered the maximum voltage.
sentences.zh: 即便如此——“学生”就在眼前，哭喊着、恳求停止——仍有百分之三十的人施加了最高电压。

sentences.en: Milgram also tried a version in which the experimenter was not in the room at all.
sentences.zh: 米尔格拉姆还试过让主试者完全不在房间里的版本。

sentences.en: The instructions were given by telephone instead.
sentences.zh: 指令改为通过电话下达。

sentences.en: Compliance dropped significantly. More people refused, and some of those who appeared to comply secretly administered lower shocks than the ones they reported.
sentences.zh: 服从率大幅下降。更多人选择了拒绝，而一些看似照做的人，实际上偷偷施加了比自己汇报的更低的电压。

sentences.en: The physical presence of the authority figure, it turned out, was an important factor.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，权威人物是否亲身在场，是一个重要因素。

sentences.en: And he tried a version in which the teacher was paired with two other "teachers", "teachers" who were presented as fellow volunteers, but were in fact actors who were instructed to refuse at critical points.
sentences.zh: 他还试过让“教师”和另外两名“教师”搭档的版本，这两人被介绍成同为志愿者的伙伴，但实际上是演员，被指示在关键节点拒绝继续。

sentences.en: And here, compliance dropped even further.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，服从率进一步下降。

sentences.en: It seemed that simply seeing someone else refuse planted the seed in the participant's head that they too could do the same thing.
sentences.zh: 看起来，仅仅是目睹别人拒绝，就在参与者心里埋下了一颗种子：原来自己也可以这样做。

sentences.en: Now, Milgram published his findings in 1963, and later in a book, Obedience to Authority, in 1974.
sentences.zh: 米尔格拉姆在1963年发表了这项研究的成果，后来又在1974年出版了专著《服从权威》(Obedience to Authority)。

sentences.en: In it, he suggested that this experiment showed that the capacity for harmful obedience to authority is not a special property of Germans in the 1930s and 40s.
sentences.zh: 在书中，他提出，这项实验表明，对权威表现出有害服从的能力，并不是20世纪三四十年代德国人独有的特质。

sentences.en: It is not unique to people with unusual psychological profiles, or to people raised in particular ideological systems.
sentences.zh: 它并非心理特征异常之人所独有，也不是在特定意识形态体系下成长起来的人才会有的东西。

sentences.en: It appears to be broadly distributed across ordinary human beings, regardless of nationality, education, or personal decency.
sentences.zh: 它似乎广泛存在于普通人之中，无关国籍、教育程度，也无关个人品行的好坏。

sentences.en: The people who administered those shocks were ordinary men and women.
sentences.zh: 那些施加电击的人，都是普普通通的男男女女。

sentences.en: Many of them were deeply distressed by what they were doing.
sentences.zh: 他们中很多人对自己正在做的事感到极度痛苦。

sentences.en: And yet they did it. Why? Well, there are a few theories about which factors contributed to this.
sentences.zh: 但他们还是做了。为什么呢？关于是哪些因素促成了这一点，有几种理论。

sentences.en: The first is something we've touched on already: the structure.
sentences.zh: 第一点，我们前面已经提到过：结构性因素。

sentences.en: There was the setting: Yale University, at first at least.
sentences.zh: 首先是场地：至少一开始，是在耶鲁大学。

sentences.en: Then, there was the authority figure. There was the scientific context.
sentences.zh: 其次是权威人物的存在，还有科学研究这一情境背景。

sentences.en: There was the graduated escalation that made each individual step seem small.
sentences.zh: 还有那种循序渐进的升级方式，让每一小步看起来都微不足道。

sentences.en: Just 15 more volts, like a frog in boiling water.
sentences.zh: 不过是再多加15伏特而已，就像“温水煮青蛙”一样。

sentences.en: And there was the physical and psychological distance from the person being harmed.
sentences.zh: 此外，还有与受害者之间物理上和心理上的距离感。

sentences.en: You were just pressing a button, you were not being forced to pick up an iron bar and beat someone with it.
sentences.zh: 你只是在按一个按钮，而不是被迫拿起一根铁棍去殴打别人。

sentences.en: Together, all of this was enough to override what people knew, somewhere inside themselves, to be wrong.
sentences.zh: 所有这些因素加在一起，足以压制住人们内心深处其实明白“这是错的”这一认知。

sentences.en: This is what Hannah Arendt believed she had seen in Eichmann, and it is what Milgram said he had demonstrated in a laboratory.
sentences.zh: 这正是汉娜·阿伦特认为自己在艾希曼身上看到的东西，也正是米尔格拉姆声称自己在实验室里证明了的东西。

sentences.en: People are deeply responsive to context, to authority, to the structures they find themselves inside, far more so than the simple categories of good and evil would suggest.
sentences.zh: 人们对所处的情境、权威以及自身所在的结构，反应之强烈，远远超出“善”与“恶”这种简单二分法所能解释的程度。

sentences.en: Now, Milgram was at pains to clarify what his findings did not mean.
sentences.zh: 不过，米尔格拉姆也一再费心澄清，他的研究结论并不意味着什么。

sentences.en: He was not saying that all humans are potential Nazis.
sentences.zh: 他并不是说，所有人都是潜在的纳粹分子。

sentences.en: He was not saying that individual character is irrelevant.
sentences.zh: 他也不是说，个人品格无关紧要。

sentences.en: Some people did refuse. Some walked out of the experiment before reaching the maximum.
sentences.zh: 确实有人拒绝了，也有人在还没加到最高电压之前就中途退出了实验。

sentences.en: What the results suggested, he said, was that obedience is far more common than we assume, and the conditions which produce it are neither rare nor exotic.
sentences.zh: 他说，这些结果所揭示的，是服从的现象远比我们以为的更普遍，而催生这种服从的条件，既不罕见，也不特殊。

sentences.en: The implication Milgram drew was a call for structural awareness.
sentences.zh: 米尔格拉姆由此得出的启示，是呼吁人们建立起对“结构性因素”的清醒认知。

sentences.en: We know what the conditions are. The authority figure.
sentences.zh: 我们已经知道这些条件是什么：权威人物的存在。

sentences.en: The institutional context. The isolation from peers who might model dissent.
sentences.zh: 制度化的情境背景，以及与可能带头表示异议的同伴相隔绝。

sentences.en: If we know all that, then we can begin to build institutions that counteract them.
sentences.zh: 如果我们了解这一切，就可以着手建立能够抵消这些因素的制度。

sentences.en: We can train people to recognise that shift when they enter it.
sentences.zh: 我们可以训练人们，在自己进入那种心理转变时能够察觉到它。

sentences.en: We can make refusal easier by making it visible.
sentences.zh: 我们也可以让拒绝这件事变得更“可见”，从而让拒绝变得更容易。

sentences.en: Obviously, this is easier said than done, but this experiment did valuable work in highlighting the conditions in which people can find themselves doing things they would not normally do.
sentences.zh: 当然，这说起来容易做起来难，但这项实验确实做了一件有价值的事：它揭示了人们会在什么样的条件下，做出平时绝不会做的事情。

sentences.en: Now, of course, the experiment has had its fair share of critics.
sentences.zh: 当然，这项实验也招致了不少批评。

sentences.en: In the immediate aftermath, it was criticised on an ethical level.
sentences.zh: 实验结束后不久，它就在伦理层面受到了批评。

sentences.en: After all, the teachers had been deeply distressed.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，那些“教师”们经历了深深的痛苦。

sentences.en: But the more important criticism was about what the findings actually meant, and whether the experiment was valid at all.
sentences.zh: 但更重要的质疑，在于这些结果究竟意味着什么，以及这项实验是否真的有效。

sentences.en: The most serious objection is that participants may not have fully believed the shocks were real.
sentences.zh: 最严重的质疑是：参与者可能并没有完全相信电击是真实的。

sentences.en: Some of them, at some level, may have suspected they were in a controlled situation where harm would not actually be allowed.
sentences.zh: 他们当中有些人，或许在某种程度上已经猜到，自己身处一个受控环境，实际上不会真的造成伤害。

sentences.en: If that is true, the compliance figures are less alarming.
sentences.zh: 如果真是如此，那这些服从率数据就没那么骇人了。

sentences.en: They mean only that ordinary people are willing to play along in what they suspect is a performance, not that they are willing to harm a stranger.
sentences.zh: 这只能说明，普通人愿意在他们怀疑是一场“表演”的情境中配合演下去，而不是说他们真的愿意伤害一个陌生人。

sentences.en: Now, to be fair to Milgram, he addressed this head-on, and he tried to figure out whether this was the case.
sentences.zh: 不过，公平地说，米尔格拉姆正面回应了这个问题，并试图弄清楚事实是否果真如此。

sentences.en: He surveyed the participants afterwards, and the majority reported that they had believed the shocks were real.
sentences.zh: 他事后对参与者进行了调查，大多数人都表示自己当时相信电击是真实的。

sentences.en: Some told him that the experience still haunted them.
sentences.zh: 有些人告诉他，这段经历至今仍萦绕在心头，挥之不去。

sentences.en: And other researchers have since examined the original transcripts and identified clear signs of real belief among most of the participants.
sentences.zh: 此后，其他研究者也查阅了原始记录，发现大多数参与者身上都有明显迹象表明，他们是真心相信这一切的。

sentences.en: In other words, they did believe they were inflicting real pain, but they did it anyway.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他们确实相信自己正在造成真实的痛苦，但他们还是做了。

sentences.en: Now, although the debate continues, Milgram's experiment is one of the most cited in the history of social psychology.
sentences.zh: 尽管争论至今仍未平息，但米尔格拉姆实验仍是社会心理学史上被引用次数最多的研究之一。

sentences.en: It has been replicated many times since, in modified and more ethically cautious forms, and the core finding has proved remarkably robust.
sentences.zh: 此后它被多次以修改过的、在伦理上更谨慎的形式重复验证，而其核心结论也被证明相当稳健可靠。

sentences.en: In 2009, a psychologist named Jerry Burger conducted a partial replication at Santa Clara University, stopping the experiment at 150 volts rather than allowing it to continue to the maximum.
sentences.zh: 2009年，心理学家杰里·伯格(Jerry Burger)在圣克拉拉大学进行了一次部分复现实验，把实验在150伏特处叫停，而不是让它一直进行到最高电压。

sentences.en: He found that around seventy per cent of participants were still willing to continue past that point, which is a figure consistent with Milgram's original results.
sentences.zh: 他发现，大约百分之七十的参与者仍愿意在这个节点之后继续下去，这一数字与米尔格拉姆最初的实验结果基本一致。

sentences.en: Now, the uncomfortable thing for anyone listening to this is that you're probably thinking some variant of "I would never do that", but what the experiment suggests is that, "well, you're probably more likely to do it than you think".
sentences.zh: 现在，对听这期节目的人来说，一个不太舒服的事实是：你大概正在想“我绝对不会那么做”之类的话，但这项实验所暗示的却是——“你做出那种事的可能性，其实比你以为的要大得多”。

sentences.en: Milgram had a term for this. He called it the " agentic state."
sentences.zh: 米尔格拉姆为此专门创造了一个术语，他称之为“代理状态”(the agentic state)。

sentences.en: It is the psychological shift from seeing yourself as a moral agent, someone who makes their own decisions, to seeing yourself as an instrument of someone else's will.
sentences.zh: 这是一种心理上的转变：从把自己视为一个能够自主做决定的道德主体，转变为把自己视为他人意志的执行工具。

sentences.en: It's what soldiers describe when they talk about following orders.
sentences.zh: 这正是士兵们在谈论“服从命令”时所描述的那种状态。

sentences.en: It's what corporate employees describe when they implement policies they find troubling but did not choose and cannot individually change.
sentences.zh: 这也是公司员工在执行那些他们觉得有问题、却并非自己选择、也无力单独改变的政策时所描述的状态。

sentences.en: In a micro way, it's what we all experience when we are asked to do something we would not do on our own initiative, but we go through with because the organisation we belong to requires it.
sentences.zh: 从微观层面来说，这也是我们每个人都体验过的：被要求去做一件自己不会主动去做的事，却因为所属的组织要求这样做，而最终照做了。

sentences.en: And Milgram is not judging us for it, or providing an answer for what to do about it.
sentences.zh: 米尔格拉姆并没有因此评判我们，也没有给出该如何应对这一点的答案。

sentences.en: What he is saying, and this experiment suggests, is that the division between good and evil is not as clear-cut as we might like to think.
sentences.zh: 他想说的是——而这项实验也表明——善与恶之间的界限，并不像我们愿意相信的那样泾渭分明。

sentences.en: OK, then, that is it for today's episode, the first part of our three-part mini-series on The Dark Side of Psychology.
sentences.zh: 好了，今天的节目就到这里，这是我们三集迷你系列《心理学的阴暗面》的第一部分。

sentences.en: Next up we'll be moving into the disturbing world of Harry Harlow's monkey experiments, where the question of what love actually is was put to the test in a primate laboratory in Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 下一集，我们将走进 Harry Harlow 猴子实验那个令人不安的世界，“爱究竟是什么”这个问题，在威斯康星州的一间灵长类实验室里接受了检验。

sentences.en: And in part three, we'll be heading to the psychiatric hospitals of 1970s America for the Rosenhan experiment, perhaps the most controversial study of all.
sentences.zh: 而在第三部分，我们将前往20世纪70年代美国的精神病院，讲述罗森汉实验(the Rosenhan experiment)——这或许是这三项研究中最具争议的一个。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期 Leonardo English 出品的 English Learning for Curious Minds。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，祝你平安，我们下期节目再见。
